insights: The dataset has 96,453 rows and 12 columns (8 numeric, 3 categorical).
Time range: 2005-12-31 to 2016-12-31 (column 'Formatted Date', used as the time index).
Constant column(s) with no information: ['Loud Cover'] - excluded from correlation, KDE and noise analysis.

missing_duplicates.description: Completeness check: missing cells per column and exact duplicate rows.
insights: 'Precip Type' has 517 missing values (0.536%) - categorical; recorded for review only (no values are filled or rows removed).
24 fully duplicated rows (0.025%); reported only, with duplicate rows retained.

dataset_specific_checks.description: Weather-specific range and zero-value checks. Suspect values are flagged for review, not silently changed.

checks.meaning: relative humidity as a fraction (0 to 1)

insights: Humidity is recorded as a fraction: 22 rows (0.0228%) are exactly 0. A true 0% relative humidity is physically possible but exceptionally dry; treat these as suspect readings and inspect their weather/date context. They are reported for review only; this analysis does not replace readings, impute values, or remove rows.

Context: 21 of 22 zero-humidity records are labeled snow; their median temperature is -15.0 °C. This suggests a cold-weather cluster worth investigating; it does not establish that the measurements are correct.
Pressure has 1,288 nonpositive readings. Zero millibars is not a plausible surface weather observation; investigate whether it is a missing-value sentinel before analysis or modeling.
Loud Cover is constant (all observed values are 0 in this dataset), so it carries no predictive information and is excluded from correlation and modeling features.

outliers.description: Extreme values flagged with two methods: IQR fences (Q1-1.5*IQR, Q3+1.5*IQR) and Z-score (|z| > 3).
insights: Most outlier-prone feature: 'Pressure (millibars)' (3284 IQR outliers, 3.451%).
No IQR outliers in: ['Wind Bearing (degrees)', 'Visibility (km)'].

noise.description: Is there noise in the data, and how much? Each numeric feature is tested for random fluctuation, isolated spikes, stuck sensors and physically impossible readings, then given a verdict.

method.noise_to_signal: Robust noise sigma (MAD of the 2nd difference / sqrt(6)) divided by the feature's robust std (MAD-based, immune to bad readings). 0 = perfectly smooth, 1 = pure random noise. Window-free, so the daily and seasonal cycles are NOT counted as noise.
method.snr_db: 10*log10(signal variance / noise variance). Above 20 dB is very clean; below 5 dB is noisy.
method.von_neumann: Mean squared step-to-step change / variance. Near 0 = smooth curve, near 2 = random.
method.spikes: Points further than 4 robust sigmas from the median of their 4 neighbours (Hampel-style, leave-one-out).
method.stuck_sensor: At least 24 identical consecutive readings on a continuous feature.
method.out_of_range: Values outside the physically possible range of the quantity.

reasons: moderate random fluctuation (noise is 33% of the signal's std)
moderate random fluctuation (noise is 17% of the signal's std)

skipped_features.reason: circular direction; linear noise and spike distances are not valid for angles

insights: YES - noise detected in 6 of 6 features: ['Temperature (C)', 'Apparent Temperature (C)', 'Humidity', 'Wind Speed (km/h)', 'Visibility (km)', 'Pressure (millibars)'].
Noisiest: 'Wind Speed (km/h)' (noise/signal 0.33); cleanest: 'Pressure (millibars)' (0.02).
'Temperature (C)': 1301 isolated spikes (1.349%).
'Apparent Temperature (C)': 1462 isolated spikes (1.516%).
'Humidity': 1077 isolated spikes (1.117%).
'Wind Speed (km/h)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 33% of the signal's std); 714 isolated spikes (0.74%).
'Visibility (km)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 17% of the signal's std); 6027 isolated spikes (6.249%); stuck at 0 for 193 consecutive readings.
'Pressure (millibars)': 2313 isolated spikes (2.431%); 1288 physically impossible values (valid range 850 to 1090).
These are diagnostic flags only. No readings are changed, imputed, or removed by this workflow.

monthly_trends.description: Monthly aggregation of every feature (mean, 10th/90th percentile, std), seasonal averages and month-by-month trend lines across the years.
insights: 'Temperature (C)' averages highest in July (22.97) and lowest in January (0.82).
'Humidity' averages highest in December (0.87) and lowest in August (0.64).
Most variable month for 'Temperature (C)': 2013-04 (std 7.22).
Most variable month for 'Humidity': 2015-08 (std 0.23).

correlation.description: Linear (Pearson) and rank (Spearman) relationships between numeric features, plus how the main variables behave for each weather 'Summary'.
insights: Very strong positive link between 'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' (r = 0.99).
Strong negative link between 'Temperature (C)' and 'Humidity' (r = -0.63).
Strong negative link between 'Apparent Temperature (C)' and 'Humidity' (r = -0.60).
'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' are nearly redundant (|r| >= 0.9) - keep one to avoid multicollinearity in a model.
'Visibility (km)' vs 'Pressure (millibars)': Pearson 0.06 but Spearman -0.13 - the relationship is monotonic but not linear (or distorted by outliers/zeros).
'Wind Speed (km/h)' vs 'Pressure (millibars)': Pearson -0.05 but Spearman -0.23 - the relationship is monotonic but not linear (or distorted by outliers/zeros).
'Temperature (C)' vs 'Pressure (millibars)': Pearson -0.01 but Spearman -0.30 - the relationship is monotonic but not linear (or distorted by outliers/zeros).
Almost independent of every other feature: ['Pressure (millibars)'].
Average 'Apparent Temperature (C)' is highest for 'Partly Cloudy' (15.39) and lowest for 'Foggy' (-0.21).
Average 'Humidity' is highest for 'Foggy' (0.95) and lowest for 'Breezy and Partly Cloudy' (0.55).
correlation.correlation_note: Correlations use the source values as stored. Missing pairs are naturally unavailable to the correlation calculation; flagged sentinel values remain included and can affect results. Circular direction columns are omitted from linear correlations. No source values are changed.

by_category.note: top 8 categories kept, the rest grouped as 'Other'
